=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md
  Line or code reference: lines 44-54 (the dispatch start prompt), and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md lines 18-19
  Problem: The Parked gate lives only in the new implement-issue-claude.md. A consumer repo whose installed implement-issue-claude.md predates the next @stable release receives the — dispatched marker in the launch prompt, ignores it, re-adds ai:claude in the old step 2 Claim gate, and proceeds with implementation. The dispatch prompt at lines 46-48 defers to /implement-issue-claude without an independent label check.
  WHY: claim_check_failed targets (consumer repos the pickup session cannot read) that lose ai:claude between the pickup read and session start will be dispatched instead of parked. The intake-side and pickup-side batch-read checks cover every other case. The gap is narrow in practice: it affects only stale-installed consumer repos whose issues the pickup cannot reach, and closes completely with the @stable sync of the same files. The dispatch prompt already handles the missing-file case by reading the template from ref stable, but not the stale-installed-file case.
  severity=low | confidence=3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md
  Line or code reference: lines 46-48
  Problem: The trigger prompt for issue dispatch passes /implement-issue-claude <url> — dispatched and relies on the session running the updated implement-issue-claude.md containing the Parked gate. However, consumer repositories retain their existing checkout copy of .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md until the next @stable release sync occurs. Because the local file is present in consumer repositories, the fallback instruction to fetch from upstream ref stable does not execute. The older installed command does not recognize — dispatched and unconditionally executes Step 2 (Claim: add ai:claude if missing).
  WHY: For consumer issues where the pickup read fails open (claim_check_failed due to an unattached proxy or 403) or where ai:claude was removed after the pickup read, the dispatched session in the consumer repository executes the pre-sync command. Step 2 in that command re-adds ai:claude via mcp__github__issue_write and proceeds with implementation instead of stopping. Adding the parked-label check directly into the launch prompt before invoking /implement-issue-claude ensures older installed commands in consumer checkouts do not re-claim parked issues during the rollout window.
  severity=high | confidence=4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md
  Line or code reference: lines 43-57, the issue launch prompt body sent to the new session via create_trigger.
  Problem: The round-2 fix moved the final claim re-check into the implementation session via the new "Parked" gate in implement-issue-claude.md step 2 and the "— dispatched" marker in this prompt, but the launch prompt still delegates every claim check to the consumer's local .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md. Consumer repos whose .claude/commands/ was installed by an earlier /seed-repo retain the OLD command (per agents.md: "`.claude/commands/` is not part of the synced surface"; the same is implied by the seed-repo/asset-set path described in agents.md item 15). The OLD command ignores the marker and unconditionally re-adds ai:claude in its existing "Claim" gate. So for those consumers, a label removed after the pickup's batch read but before the session starts still re-adds ai:claude and proceeds, defeating the park. The intake-side (claim_label_refusal in authorize_target) and pickup-side (apply_dispatch_claim_check) checks are coding-workflows-side and unaffected; only the round-2 session-side check is consumer-side and has this gap.
  WHY: For any consumer with the OLD .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md (most consumers that ran /seed-repo before this PR — .claude/ is not part of the @stable sync, so those files stay installed until the consumer re-runs /seed-repo or manually copies the new twin), the dispatched session follows the local "Claim" gate, re-adds ai:claude, and proceeds with implementation. The PR description's headline ("Removing `ai:claude` from a queued issue now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it") and the changelog fragment's identical headline do not hold for those consumers. The README and agents.md also describe the behavior as unconditional ("with that marker `/implement-issue-claude` step 2 stops as `issue parked`"), so operators reading them after merge will believe the headline applies to every consumer.
  severity=high | confidence=5
- Requirement: "Removing `ai:claude` from a queued issue now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it." (PR description headline; identical sentence is the changelog fragment's lead and the agents.md item 15 update.)
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md, inside the issue launch prompt body (current lines 43-46, before the /implement-issue-claude invocation).
  Evidence of absence: The launch prompt invokes `/implement-issue-claude <url> — dispatched` and delegates every claim behaviour to the consumer's local .claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md. The Copilot review comment 4166656306 (posted 2026-10-02T14:27:02Z, after the round-2 commit 252907df at 14:23:24Z) explicitly asked for "the parked-label stop directly in this launch prompt so it also overrides older installed commands"; the round-2 fix did not act on that — only the marker was added, no claim check inside the launch prompt. The cross-pollination summary records 4 of 6 reviewer slots flagging the same defect at confidence 4-5: google_gemini-3_8-flash ("Consumer repositories retain their installed `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` until the next `@stable` release sync"), openai_gpt-6-luna ("The parked-label gate only works when the consumer has the updated implementation command"), qwen_qwen3.7-plus ("Consumer repos retain their installed implement-issue-claude.md until the next @stable sync"), and minimax_minimax-m3 as a TASK_GAP. The minimum fix is a 3-5 line pre-flight in the launch prompt itself: read the live issue (gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N> --jq '.labels[].name'), check that ai:claude is present, and stop with an explicit report when it is not — before invoking /implement-issue-claude. That makes the park survive regardless of which twin the consumer has installed. The new test test_dispatched_session_stops_when_the_claim_was_removed reads only the workflow-templates twin (TEMPLATE_COMMANDS / "claude-issue-dispatch.md") and never asserts that the prompt itself contains a claim check; a sibling test that stages an OLD implement-issue-claude.md locally would catch the rollout-window scenario, and the existing test would need to extend its string assertion to cover the prompt-side pre-flight once it lands.
  severity=high | confidence=5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md
  Line or code reference: lines 46-54 (the issue dispatch prompt)
  Problem: The parked-label gate only takes effect when the consumer repository has synced the updated `implement-issue-claude.md`. Consumer repos retain their installed `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` until the next `@stable` sync. During that rollout window, the old installed command does not recognize the `— dispatched` marker and unconditionally re-adds `ai:claude` in Step 2 "Claim", so a label removed after the pickup's batch read (or a `claim_check_failed` consumer target) still proceeds with implementation.
  WHY: The dispatch prompt passes `— dispatched` to `/implement-issue-claude`, but the old installed command ignores the marker and follows the unconditional Claim instruction. The launch prompt itself carries no parked-label stop, so it cannot override the old installed command. The PR's headline claim ("Removing `ai:claude` from a queued issue now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it") is unconditional, but the session-side re-check is rollout-bound. The fix is to add an explicit parked-label check to the launch prompt before invoking `/implement-issue-claude`, so the check applies even when the session falls back to an older installed command.
  severity=high | confidence=5
- Requirement: "Removing `ai:claude` from an issue that is already queued now stops the Claude issue pickup from starting it" (PR description headline, changelog fragment headline)
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md (the dispatch launch prompt, before the `/implement-issue-claude` invocation)
  Evidence of absence: The PR description's headline claim and changelog entry are unconditional, but consumer repos keep their installed `implement-issue-claude.md` until the next `@stable` sync. The LAST RUN DIFF (commit `252907df`) adds the `— dispatched` marker to the dispatch prompt and the Parked gate to the `implement-issue-claude.md` twin, neither of which is enforced for consumer repos running an older installed command. The launch prompt itself carries no parked-label stop that would override the old installed command.
